title: GWAS identifies a functional MSTN variant associated with higher lean mass in humans
summary: A genome-wide association meta-analysis of DXA-derived lean mass in about 79,000 people identified 63 loci, including a rare MSTN variant associated with higher leg lean mass. Supervised deep residual convolutional networks imputed missing DXA/MRI image-derived phenotypes from raw images for UK Biobank association analyses; statistical GWAS and researcher-led assays supplied the genetic and functional evidence. The findings are observational, largely from European-ancestry participants, and do not establish clinical benefit from myostatin inhibition.
ai_technology: Supervised deep residual convolutional neural networks for DXA/MRI image-derived phenotype imputation

evidence.tested: Deep residual convolutional networks were trained on labeled DXA/MRI images with an 80/20 train/validation split; imputed phenotypes were used in GWAS. The main association analysis used BOLT-LMM; the paper also reports functional characterization of MSTN p.Ile225Thr.
evidence.unknown: The paper does not establish causal clinical benefit from myostatin inhibition; imputed phenotypes and observational genetic associations have limitations.
evidence.ai_role: Supervised deep residual convolutional networks imputed missing image-derived phenotypes from raw DXA and MRI images, increasing phenotype availability for the GWAS; the genetic association model and functional assays were separate statistical and experimental analyses.

source_review.scope: Publisher abstract, Results, UK Biobank imaging-processing Methods, Discussion limitations and publication metadata.
